title: Template Specialization Basics
learningObjectives: Identify template parameters and required operations.
Design a reusable generic utility or type.

understand.concept: Specialization tailors a template for a particular type or pattern. Full specialization selects exact arguments; partial specialization matches patterns for class templates. Use sparingly.
understand.whyItMatters: Exceptional behavior can be adapted without losing the generic interface.
understand.explain: Use a generic primary template where possible; specialize only when type-specific behavior is needed. Prefer overloads for many function-template cases.

examples.title: Full specialization
examples.code: template<class T>struct Tag{static constexpr int code=0;};\ntemplate<>struct Tag<bool>{static constexpr int code=1;};
examples.explanation: bool gets a specialized class-template definition.

examples.title: Function overload
examples.code: template<class T>void print(T v){std::cout<<v;}\nvoid print(bool v){std::cout<<(v?\"true\":\"false\");}
examples.explanation: Non-template overload may be selected for bool.

examples.title: Partial class specialization
examples.code: template<class T>struct Info{static constexpr bool ptr=false;};\ntemplate<class T>struct Info<T*>{static constexpr bool ptr=true;};

examples.title: Keep generic implementation
examples.explanation: No specialization needed when operation works for all compatible types.

examples.title: Specialized printer pattern
examples.code: template<class T>struct Printer{static void show(const T& v){std::cout<<v;}};
examples.explanation: A specialization can adapt behavior for a particular type.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze each Template Specialization Basics example: identify parameters, requirements, deduced or explicit arguments, and instantiated behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a generic C++ utility or type demonstrating template specialization basics. Test two supported types, one boundary case, and one unsupported/constrained type; explain why it is or is not accepted.
hints: Begin with a concrete example before generalizing.
Name template parameters for their roles.

questions.explanation: Partial specialization is for class templates.
Overloading may be simpler than specialization.

options: When tailored behavior is genuinely needed
questions.answer: When tailored behavior is genuinely needed
